text:
Matthew Tkachuk has turned into a passer who happens to have a mean streak. He has 25 assists and only four goals in 21 games, 17 of his 29 points on the power play, and a seven-game point streak with nine assists and no goals. On Saturday the Blues honored his father, Keith, in St. Louis, and Matthew picked up another assist in a Florida win.

The reunion with his brother is the headline of the Panthers' season, and the numbers say it works: Florida takes 57% of the expected goals (the quality of chances) at five on five with Matthew on the ice, almost eight points better than when he sits. Last season, when he played only 31 games, Evolving-Hockey had him barely above replacement. This version looks nothing like that.

The goals will come back toward normal. He's shooting 9% against a usual range near 13%, with the chances to match. His ice time has dipped by about a minute and a half over the last ten, which is worth watching on a deep team, but at more than four points per 60 minutes he is among the league's most productive forwards.
